dedupe_keys.name: vietnam mekong delta flood reliable network design for collecting and treating agricultural waste

description: This case study designs a network for collecting, transporting and treating agricultural waste, so that crop residues are turned into biomass energy instead of being burned in fields, while limiting the risk that floods cut roads and facilities. The authors, researchers at Loughborough University, the University of Bedfordshire and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, formulated a reliable two-stage location problem as a mixed-integer nonlinear programme that locates storage sites and treatment facilities and minimises expected disruption cost, transformed it into a quadratic programme using probability chains, and developed a two-stage method and a math-heuristic for large instances; the work is published as an open-access journal article. Case studies are in the Vietnam Mekong Delta. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: flood disruption probabilities and costs are model inputs, and the article reports solution efficiency more than a field plan. The study showed that the solution methods find optimal or near-optimal designs of the reliable network within reasonable computing time. Simulation uses: an optimisation template for waste collection networks exposed to flood disruption. Related records: the southern New Jersey landfill flood study (case_study-southern-new-jersey-landfills-flood-vulnerability-climate) assesses flood exposure of waste facilities.
